Enki.fact: At the beginning of the text, the story is set in Dilmun. The goddess of Dilmun, Ninsikila, complains to Enki that her land lacks water.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Some scholars identify _____ as another name of Ninhursag in this myth
Enki.fact: The goddess of Dilmun, Ninsikila, complains to Enki that her land lacks water. Some scholars identify Ninsikila as another name of Ninhursag in this myth.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: The next scene takes place in the marshes in the south of _____
Enki.fact: The next scene takes place in the marshes in the south of Sumer.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: After nine days of gestation, she gives birth to _____/Ninšar
Enki.fact: After nine days of gestation, she gives birth to Ninnisig/Ninšar. One day, Enki spots Ninnisig/Ninšar along the riverbank in the marsh.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: He also sleeps with her, she becomes pregnant, and after nine days of gestation, she gives birth to _____
Enki.fact: He also sleeps with her, she becomes pregnant, and after nine days of gestation, she gives birth to Ninkurra.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: In a variant of the story, she instead gives birth to _____, who is the one to give birth to Uttu
Enki.fact: In a variant of the story, she instead gives birth to Ninimma, who is the one to give birth to Uttu.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Ninhursag removes his semen from _____'s body, and grows eight plants from it
Enki.fact: Enki brings them to Uttu, introducing himself as the gardener, and she opens her house to him. Ninhursag removes his semen from Uttu's body, and grows eight plants from it.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: As a result, _____ curses him, and he falls deathly ill
Enki.fact: Ninhursag removes his semen from Uttu's body, and grows eight plants from it. As a result, Ninhursag curses him, and he falls deathly ill.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: A fox offers its help to Enlil and the other gods, and Enlil promises it fame and to erect two kiskanu trees in its honor if it succeeds in bringing _____ back
Enki.fact: Ninhursag removes his semen from Uttu's body, and grows eight plants from it. As a result, Ninhursag curses him, and he falls deathly ill.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: The fox adorns itself and goes to see _____
Enki.fact: As a result, Ninhursag curses him, and he falls deathly ill. A fox offers its help to Enlil and the other gods, and Enlil promises it fame and to erect two kiskanu trees in its honor if it succeeds in bringing Ninhursag back.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Some scholars have interpreted _____ as a premature or not fully developed baby
Enki.fact: Due to the damage to this section of the text, Enki's answer and the resolution of the myth is unclear, but it seems that he attempts to appease Ninmah and that he finds a place for Umul. Some scholars have interpreted Umul as a premature or not fully developed baby.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: It has been suggested to date to the reign of _____ I, though there is no secure evidence for its date of composition
Enki.fact: It has been suggested to date to the reign of Nebuchadnezzar I, though there is no secure evidence for its date of composition.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: The beginning of the poem describes the creation of the first gods as a result of the mingling of _____ and Abzû
Enki.fact: The beginning of the poem describes the creation of the first gods as a result of the mingling of Tiamat and Abzû. While Abzû is usually the name of Ea's underground cosmic water domain, it appears here as the personification of these waters and as Tiamat's consort.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: The clamor and restless behaviour of the younger gods angers Abzû and _____
Enki.fact: The beginning of the poem describes the creation of the first gods as a result of the mingling of Tiamat and Abzû. While Abzû is usually the name of Ea's underground cosmic water domain, it appears here as the personification of these waters and as Tiamat's consort.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: While Tiamat is initially reluctant to harm her creations, Abzû plots to kill the younger gods, supported by his vizier, _____
Enki.fact: While Tiamat is initially reluctant to harm her creations, Abzû plots to kill the younger gods, supported by his vizier, Mummu. He fashions a sleep spell that he casts on Abzû and Mummu.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: He fashions a sleep spell that he casts on Abzû and _____
Enki.fact: While Tiamat is initially reluctant to harm her creations, Abzû plots to kill the younger gods, supported by his vizier, Mummu. He fashions a sleep spell that he casts on Abzû and Mummu.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: When they are asleep, he binds and then kills Abzû, and imprisons _____
Enki.fact: While Tiamat is initially reluctant to harm her creations, Abzû plots to kill the younger gods, supported by his vizier, Mummu. He fashions a sleep spell that he casts on Abzû and Mummu.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: The following section deals with the birth of Marduk, Ea's son with _____, described as surpassing all of the gods
Enki.fact: The following section deals with the birth of Marduk, Ea's son with Damkina, described as surpassing all of the gods.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: The waves that _____ creates by whirling the winds irritate a group of gods only specified as children of Tiamat
Enki.fact: The following section deals with the birth of Marduk, Ea's son with Damkina, described as surpassing all of the gods. The waves that Marduk creates by whirling the winds irritate a group of gods only specified as children of Tiamat.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: She raises an army and takes the god _____ as her new consort
Enki.fact: She raises an army and takes the god Qingu as her new consort.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: When Ea learns of her preparations, he is horrified and brings the news to his grandfather _____
Enki.fact: When Ea learns of her preparations, he is horrified and brings the news to his grandfather Anshar. Anshar is initially angered and blames Ea for the situation caused by his murder of Abzû.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Anshar then orders Ea to defeat _____
Enki.fact: Anshar then orders Ea to defeat Tiamat. Ea then summons his son and instructs him to seek out Anshar and volunteer to challenge Tiamat.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: He fails, and _____ then sends Anu, who also fails
Enki.fact: Anshar is initially angered and blames Ea for the situation caused by his murder of Abzû. Anshar then orders Ea to defeat Tiamat.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Ea then summons his son and instructs him to seek out _____ and volunteer to challenge Tiamat
Enki.fact: Anshar then orders Ea to defeat Tiamat. He fails, and Anshar then sends Anu, who also fails.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: After his defeat of _____, Marduk organizes the universe
Enki.fact: Ea then summons his son and instructs him to seek out Anshar and volunteer to challenge Tiamat. After his defeat of Tiamat, Marduk organizes the universe.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: The rebellious gods single out _____
Enki.fact: The rebellious gods single out Qingu.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: In the last sections dealing with _____'s multiples names, Ea gives to his son his own name, and puts him in charge of his offices
Enki.fact: In the last sections dealing with Marduk's multiples names, Ea gives to his son his own name, and puts him in charge of his offices.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: He is depicted bringing the waters of the land together and organizing them, giving the Tigris and _____ their places and laying down irrigation ditches
Enki.fact: He is depicted bringing the waters of the land together and organizing them, giving the Tigris and Euphrates their places and laying down irrigation ditches.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: The task of working falls to the _____ gods
Enki.fact: The task of working falls to the Igigi gods.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: They set fire to their tools and surround Enlil's Ekur shrine in _____
Enki.fact: They set fire to their tools and surround Enlil's Ekur shrine in Nippur.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Enlil is woken up by his vizier _____, who informs him of the situation
Enki.fact: Enlil is woken up by his vizier Nusku, who informs him of the situation.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: The mother goddess is congratulated and named "_____ of all gods", Bēlet-kāla-ilī
Enki.fact: The mother goddess is congratulated and named "Mistress of all gods", Bēlet-kāla-ilī.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: In the next section of the myth, mankind has multiplied, and they create so much noise that _____ is unable to sleep
Enki.fact: In the next section of the myth, mankind has multiplied, and they create so much noise that Enlil is unable to sleep.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Humans multiply, and once again _____ is unable to sleep due to the noise
Enki.fact: Humans multiply, and once again Enlil is unable to sleep due to the noise.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: He decides this time to wipe out humanity with a famine and orders _____, the weather-god, to withhold his rain
Enki.fact: He decides this time to wipe out humanity with a famine and orders Adad, the weather-god, to withhold his rain. Once more Atra-ḫasīs prays to Enki, who instructs him to tell his fellow men to stop praying and sending offerings to all of the gods, and to instead concentrate their offerings on Adad.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: On the seventh day the flood comes and wipes out humanity, with the exception of _____-ḫasīs and his family on the boat
Enki.fact: Atra-ḫasīs speaks with his elders and explains his departure by telling them that since Enki had a falling out with Enlil, he, as Enki's servant, must leave Enlil's earth. On the seventh day the flood comes and wipes out humanity, with the exception of Atra-ḫasīs and his family on the boat.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: When the flood ends, _____-ḫasīs makes an offering to the gods
Enki.fact: On the seventh day the flood comes and wipes out humanity, with the exception of Atra-ḫasīs and his family on the boat. When the flood ends, Atra-ḫasīs makes an offering to the gods.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: As the oldest fragment preserving this myth dates from around the same period as the tablets preserving _____-ḫasīs, the relation between the two texts is uncertain
Enki.fact: As the oldest fragment preserving this myth dates from around the same period as the tablets preserving Atra-ḫasīs, the relation between the two texts is uncertain.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: The flood story in the Epic of _____ is believed to be based on the one in Atra-ḫasīs
Enki.fact: The flood story in the Epic of Gilgamesh is believed to be based on the one in Atra-ḫasīs. Gilgamesh meets the flood survivor, here named Utnapishtim, during his quest for immortality.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Gilgamesh meets the flood survivor, here named _____, during his quest for immortality
Enki.fact: Gilgamesh meets the flood survivor, here named Utnapishtim, during his quest for immortality. Utnapishtim tells him how he and his wife survived the flood and were made immortal by the gods as a result.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Ea, who did not wish to see mankind destroyed, found a way around his oath and warned _____
Enki.fact: Utnapishtim tells him how he and his wife survived the flood and were made immortal by the gods as a result. Ea, who did not wish to see mankind destroyed, found a way around his oath and warned Utnapishtim.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: With the help of his people, _____ built a massive boat that he filled with his kin, possessions, and animals
Enki.fact: Ea, who did not wish to see mankind destroyed, found a way around his oath and warned Utnapishtim. When Utnapishtim asked him what to tell the elders and the people of his city of Shuruppak, Ea instructed him to tell them that since he had fallen out with Enlil, he could not remain on the earth and that he was going to live in Ea's underground ocean.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: When the flood stopped, _____ sent three birds to see if the waters had decreased enough for him to land
Enki.fact: With the help of his people, Utnapishtim built a massive boat that he filled with his kin, possessions, and animals. When the flood stopped, Utnapishtim sent three birds to see if the waters had decreased enough for him to land.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: This episode has been compared to a similar one in the account of the flood related in the Book of _____
Enki.fact: This episode has been compared to a similar one in the account of the flood related in the Book of Genesis.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: After the last bird failed to come back to the boat, _____ prepared an offering for the gods on the top of the mountain
Enki.fact: When the flood stopped, Utnapishtim sent three birds to see if the waters had decreased enough for him to land. After the last bird failed to come back to the boat, Utnapishtim prepared an offering for the gods on the top of the mountain.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Ea told _____ that his decision to wipe out humanity was a disproportionate punishment, and proposed other ways to control the size of its population
Enki.fact: When Enlil realized that humans still lived, he was furious, and demanded to know the reason for their survival. Ea told Enlil that his decision to wipe out humanity was a disproportionate punishment, and proposed other ways to control the size of its population.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Enlil, convinced to let humanity live, granted _____ and his wife immortality
Enki.fact: Enlil, convinced to let humanity live, granted Utnapishtim and his wife immortality.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Berossos transmitted a variant of the _____ story of the flood in his Babyloniaca, a work meant to present the history of the Babylonians to the Greeks
Enki.fact: Berossos transmitted a variant of the Mesopotamian story of the flood in his Babyloniaca, a work meant to present the history of the Babylonians to the Greeks.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: His original work is lost, but it is known from quotes of _____ and Abydenus, themselves quoted by Eusebius
Enki.fact: His original work is lost, but it is known from quotes of Alexander Polyhistor and Abydenus, themselves quoted by Eusebius.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: There Kronos warns _____ (the hellenized form of the sumerian Ziusudra) about the incoming flood, appearing to him in a dream in the version quoted by Polyhistor
Enki.fact: There Kronos warns Xisuthros (the hellenized form of the sumerian Ziusudra) about the incoming flood, appearing to him in a dream in the version quoted by Polyhistor.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: He tells him the exact month in which the flood will come, and also instructs him to bury all writings in _____, two details which are not present in the older cuneiform sources
Enki.fact: He tells him the exact month in which the flood will come, and also instructs him to bury all writings in Sippar, two details which are not present in the older cuneiform sources.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Inanna takes them and loads them into the Boat of _____, and she departs for her city of Uruk
Enki.fact: Inanna takes them and loads them into the Boat of Heaven, and she departs for her city of Uruk. Enki's reaction is missing due to the fragmentary of the text at this point, but determined to get back the me-s, he dispatches Isimud and enkum servants to seize the Boat of Heaven and its cargo.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: He asks _____ where they are, and the sukkal replies that he has given them all to Inanna
Enki.fact: He asks Isimud where they are, and the sukkal replies that he has given them all to Inanna. Enki's reaction is missing due to the fragmentary of the text at this point, but determined to get back the me-s, he dispatches Isimud and enkum servants to seize the Boat of Heaven and its cargo.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: As soon as the enkums grab the Boat, Inanna summons her sukkal _____, who prevents them from seizing it in unclear circumstances
Enki.fact: As soon as the enkums grab the Boat, Inanna summons her sukkal Ninshubur, who prevents them from seizing it in unclear circumstances. Each time, Inanna calls Ninshubur and the Boat of Heaven is able to continue its journey.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Each time, Inanna calls _____ and the Boat of Heaven is able to continue its journey
Enki.fact: As soon as the enkums grab the Boat, Inanna summons her sukkal Ninshubur, who prevents them from seizing it in unclear circumstances. Each time, Inanna calls Ninshubur and the Boat of Heaven is able to continue its journey.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Inanna eventually reaches _____ triumphantly and unloads the me-s among the celebration of her people
Enki.fact: The second time, he dispatches Isimud alongside the fifty giants of Eridu, the third time alongside the fifty Lahamu of the Engur, the fourth time alongside the "Big fish", the fifth time alongside the guards of Uruk, and the sixth time alongside the guards of the Turungal canal. Inanna eventually reaches Uruk triumphantly and unloads the me-s among the celebration of her people.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: The queen of the _____, Ereshkigal, is displeased to learn of Inanna's visit
Enki.fact: In the Sumerian version, as Inanna makes her preparations to journey into the Underworld, she instructs her sukkal Ninshubur to ask Enlil, Nanna, and Enki for help if something happens to her. The queen of the Underworld, Ereshkigal, is displeased to learn of Inanna's visit.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: When Inanna is brought into her presence, _____ strikes her down and hangs her corpse from a nail
Enki.fact: The queen of the Underworld, Ereshkigal, is displeased to learn of Inanna's visit. When Inanna is brought into her presence, Ereshkigal strikes her down and hangs her corpse from a nail.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Ninshubur, in mourning, goes to see _____ and Nanna, but both of them refuse to help her
Enki.fact: In the Sumerian version, as Inanna makes her preparations to journey into the Underworld, she instructs her sukkal Ninshubur to ask Enlil, Nanna, and Enki for help if something happens to her. Ninshubur, in mourning, goes to see Enlil and Nanna, but both of them refuse to help her.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: He then tells them to go see _____, who is in labour, and to express sympathy
Enki.fact: He then tells them to go see Ereshkigal, who is in labour, and to express sympathy.

Enki.question: Finally they are to sprinkle the food of life and the water of life upon it to revive _____
Enki.fact: Finally they are to sprinkle the food of life and the water of life upon it to revive Inanna. The plan succeeds, and Inanna is able to leave the Underworld, though she then has to find a substitute to take her place there.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: The plan succeeds, and _____ is able to leave the Underworld, though she then has to find a substitute to take her place there
Enki.fact: Finally they are to sprinkle the food of life and the water of life upon it to revive Inanna. The plan succeeds, and Inanna is able to leave the Underworld, though she then has to find a substitute to take her place there.

Enki.fact: She picks her husband Dumuzi, who, unlike her attendants, was not mourning her properly.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: In the _____ version, it is Papsukkal that comes to see the gods with the news that since Ishtar has been trapped in the Underworld, all sexual activity has ceased on earth
Enki.fact: In the Akkadian version, it is Papsukkal that comes to see the gods with the news that since Ishtar has been trapped in the Underworld, all sexual activity has ceased on earth.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Ea creates _____, an androgynous figure, and instructs them to appease Ereshkigal, and then to have her swear an oath of the great gods to give them the water of life
Enki.fact: Ea creates Asushunamir, an androgynous figure, and instructs them to appease Ereshkigal, and then to have her swear an oath of the great gods to give them the water of life. Ishtar is revived, but Ereshkigal is furious and she curses Asushunamir to a grim life on earth.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Ishtar is revived, but _____ is furious and she curses Asushunamir to a grim life on earth
Enki.fact: Ea creates Asushunamir, an androgynous figure, and instructs them to appease Ereshkigal, and then to have her swear an oath of the great gods to give them the water of life. Ishtar is revived, but Ereshkigal is furious and she curses Asushunamir to a grim life on earth.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Here the god appears in his usual role in _____ literature as an ingenious deity who devises plans to resolve difficult situations
Enki.fact: Here the god appears in his usual role in Mesopotamian literature as an ingenious deity who devises plans to resolve difficult situations.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: The poem begins with a hymn praising _____ in her aspect as the goddess of war
Enki.fact: Ishtar is revived, but Ereshkigal is furious and she curses Asushunamir to a grim life on earth. The poem begins with a hymn praising Ishtar in her aspect as the goddess of war.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Ea then tells Ṣaltu that she has been created to disrespectfully challenge _____, whom he calls Irnina ( the name of one of her aspects) and he instructs her on how she is to act
Enki.fact: Ea then tells Ṣaltu that she has been created to disrespectfully challenge Ishtar, whom he calls Irnina ( the name of one of her aspects) and he instructs her on how she is to act. He proceeds to describe Ishtar so that Ṣaltu might recognize her.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: He proceeds to describe _____ so that Ṣaltu might recognize her
Enki.fact: Ea then tells Ṣaltu that she has been created to disrespectfully challenge Ishtar, whom he calls Irnina ( the name of one of her aspects) and he instructs her on how she is to act. He proceeds to describe Ishtar so that Ṣaltu might recognize her.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: In a fragmentary section, Ea taunts Ṣaltu by praising _____
Enki.fact: Ea then tells Ṣaltu that she has been created to disrespectfully challenge Ishtar, whom he calls Irnina ( the name of one of her aspects) and he instructs her on how she is to act. He proceeds to describe Ishtar so that Ṣaltu might recognize her.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: Ishtar hears of this new opponent and dispatches her sukkal Ninshubur to acquire more information on her.

Enki.fact: In a fragmentary section, Ea taunts Ṣaltu by praising Ishtar. Ishtar hears of this new opponent and dispatches her sukkal Ninshubur to acquire more information on her.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: In the last section, the goddess, now referred to with the name _____, complains to Ea about Ṣaltu and demands that he sends her away
Enki.fact: In the last section, the goddess, now referred to with the name Agushaya, complains to Ea about Ṣaltu and demands that he sends her away.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: The confrontation between Ishtar and Ṣaltu is lost. The end of the poem indicates that Ishtar has abandoned her overly violent ways.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: The god then embarks on the journey to _____ on his boat
Enki.fact: The god then embarks on the journey to Nippur on his boat. In preparation of the banquet that he is to hold in Nippur, Enki kills oxen and sheep, and brings musical instruments with him.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: When he arrives in _____, he enters the giguna (a sacred part of a temple) and begins to prepare the beer for the banquet
Enki.fact: The god then embarks on the journey to Nippur on his boat. In preparation of the banquet that he is to hold in Nippur, Enki kills oxen and sheep, and brings musical instruments with him.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: An and _____ are seated in the high place, and Nintu is seated at a place of honor
Enki.fact: An and Enlil are seated in the high place, and Nintu is seated at a place of honor. At the end of the composition, Enlil, pleased by the banquet, gives a blessing praising Enki's temple.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Some scholars argue that lines 136–155 are not the evocation of the spell of _____, and that they are therefore not part of Enmerkar's speech
Enki.fact: Some scholars argue that lines 136–155 are not the evocation of the spell of Nudimmud, and that they are therefore not part of Enmerkar's speech.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: An unification of the languages, but taking place in the past, has also been proposed by _____
Enki.fact: An unification of the languages, but taking place in the past, has also been proposed by Christoph Uehlinger.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Under his advice, the gods summon _____'s mother Mami, cover her with honors, name her ''Mistress of all the gods'', Belet-ili, and name her son Ninurta champion of the gods
Enki.fact: Under his advice, the gods summon Ninurta's mother Mami, cover her with honors, name her ''Mistress of all the gods'', Belet-ili, and name her son Ninurta champion of the gods. Ninurta confronts the Anzû bird, however, he is able to use the powers of the tablets to deflect the arrows that Ninurta shoots at him.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Ninurta sends _____ back to Ea to ask for help
Enki.fact: Ninurta sends Sharur back to Ea to ask for help.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: He lures _____ to this location, and pretends to be ignorant of the situation when he is attacked by the turtle
Enki.fact: Unhappy with his promises, Ninurta begins to secretly plot against Enki, who becomes aware of his plans. After Ninurta raises his hand against Enki's sukkal Isimud in an altercation, Enki fashions a turtle from the clay of the Abzû and stations it next to the gates of the Abzu.
